title: ELIXIR: Learning from User Feedback on Explanations to Improve Recommender Models
abstract: System-provided explanations for recommendations are an important component towards transparent and trustworthy AI. In state-of-the-art research, this is a one-way signal, though, to improve user acceptance. In this paper, we turn the role of explanations around and investigate how they can contribute to enhancing the quality of generated recommendations themselves. We devise a human-in-the-loop framework, called Elixir, where user feedback on explanations is leveraged for pairwise learning of user preferences. Elixir leverages feedback on pairs of recommendations and explanations to learn user-specific latent preference vectors, overcoming sparseness by label propagation with item-similarity-based neighborhoods. Our framework is instantiated using generalized graph recommendation via Random Walk with Restart. Insightful experiments with a real user study show significant improvements in movie and book recommendations over item-level feedback.

title: Harnessing the Synergy Between Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain for Enhancing Transparency Security
venue_or_source: 2024 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Innovations in High Speed Communication and Signal Processing (IHCSP)
abstract: In the recommended technique, AI and blockchain technology improve system stability and projected maintenance. This innovative technique begins with sensor data collection and preprocessing. This covers cleaning, normalizing, and extracting characteristics for AI model training. The model’s projections set alarming limitations. These are securely stored on a blockchain for data transparency. Continuous feedback loops make data processing safer and enhance model prediction. Combining monitor data with model projections to identify problems and provide effective solutions makes the system more trustworthy. Adaptive beamforming improves optical communication by changing beamforming weights and channel responses in real time, enhancing signal integrity and performance. The technique enhances transparency, security, automation efficiency, scalability, portability, data integrity, privacy protection, system speed, resource usage, fault tolerance, cost-effectiveness, and user experience. Simple, safe, and effective system management and predictive maintenance are demonstrated by their consistently higher performance than prior methods. AI and blockchain work together to establish a new standard by eliminating current constraints and changing all elements.

title: Iterative Chain-of-Thought: Self-Correcting Reasoning via Verifier-Guided Feedback Loop
abstract: SUMMARY & CONCLUSIONSLarge language models often produce logically flawed reasoning despite generating correct final answers, which limits their trustworthiness in high-stakes applications. This limitation is problematic in reliability-critical systems where both accuracy and verifiable reasoning are essential. This paper presents Iterative Chain-of-Thought Refinement, a lightweight framework employing a fine-tuned verifier to detect and provide targeted feedback on logic errors, guiding the model through iterative self-correction, without modifying the frozen base generator.This implementation uses a fine-tuned Gemma-2B [10] verifier to evaluate a LLaMA-3B [12] generator's reasoning chains, creating a feedback loop that terminates when reasoning becomes fully valid or reaches maximum iterations. Evaluations on the GSM8K [7] and REVEAL [11] benchmarks showed strong improvements in the proportion of valid reasoning chains, rising from 71.7% to 93.5% and from 58.3% to 89.6%, respectively, achieved with minimal computational overhead averaging less than two refinement iterations per problem. These gains were accompanied by improvements in coherence, readability, and conciseness.This is particularly relevant in reliability engineering contexts, where flawed diagnostic inference can compromise system safety and lead to suboptimal maintenance decisions. In reliability-critical domains, practitioners must trace through complex failure mode analyses, root cause investigations, and risk assessments where each logical step must be verifiable and defensible. For instance, in failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA), incorrect reasoning about failure propagation can lead to underestimated risk ratings, inadequate mitigation strategies, and potential safety incidents. Similarly, predictive maintenance systems increasingly rely on AI-driven diagnostic reasoning to recommend maintenance actions, where erroneous logical steps could result in unnecessary downtime or, more critically, missed failure predictions that compromise system integrity.

title: Rethinking Fairness in LLM-Based Recommender Systems: A Survey
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are reshaping recommender systems by enabling more semantic, generative, and interactive recommendation pipelines. However, this shift also introduces new fairness challenges, as biases may arise from pretrained knowledge, prompts, generated explanations, decoding strategies, and feedback loops. This survey provides a systematic review of fairness in LLM-based recommender systems (LLM4Rec), organizing existing studies through a two-dimensional view of bias mechanisms and fairness targets, together with a structured overview of the evaluation landscape and mitigation strategies. We further connect fairness with broader trustworthy concerns, including explainability, privacy, robustness, and controllability. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first survey specifically focused on fairness in LLM4Rec, aiming to provide a structured foundation for future research on comprehensive and reliable fairness evaluation in LLM4Rec.
